rationale: Two tasks reviewed via blind, edge-case, and acceptance lenses on the full diff. Both EPMCDME-15582's four story ACs and the plan's explicit requirements are implemented and match the Jira regression scenario's intent. One decision_needed finding (CR-001): the edge-case and blind lenses independently flagged that the EPMCDME-17201 fix's one-message lookahead (`nextMessageSkillName(messages[i+1])`) checks only the literal next array element, with no skip over intervening isMeta/isSidechain lines; this codebase's own conversation-splitter logic (claude.conversations-processor.ts) treats such interposed lines as a known, recurring phenomenon in real transcripts, so there is a real (not merely theoretical) chance the dedup silently fails to fire on some real sessions shaped differently from the synthetic test fixtures, which never include an interposed line. One patch finding (CR-002): Task 1's plan explicitly promised (Review Focus) a test proving a <command-name> tag without its <command-message> sibling is not treated as a genuine wrapper 'in either fix'; the pre-existing matchCommandNames gate is covered by an untouched prior test, but the new wrappedCommandName/countTurns path has no such test, even though inspection shows the guard is implemented correctly. 8 other concerns raised by the lenses were triaged out: LOCAL_ONLY_COMMANDS cross-repo drift is an explicit, user-approved, documented design tradeoff (mirrors the already-shipped backend precedent); wrappedCommandName's first-match-only behavior and recordCommand's one-command-per-message assumption are consistent with this codebase's own documented invariant that a genuine wrapper is exactly one command per user turn, making multi-command lines effectively unreachable; case-sensitivity mismatch between a command name and its dispatched skill name is unlikely since both derive from the same slug; the turns-metric historical-inconsistency concern is the expected, intended effect of fixing a counting bug (same situation as the already-shipped backend fix) and is explicitly out of scope per the plan's Global Constraints; the '/model nuance' concern directly contradicts the ticket's own acceptance criterion #3; the missing combined end-to-end regression test and the missing 'plain prompt unaffected by unrelated Skill call' test are both nice-to-haves not required by the plan's Review Focus (the latter is structurally guaranteed since matchCommandNames returns [] for non-wrapper text, so recordCommand is never invoked on it).

findings.problem: The EPMCDME-17201 dedup only checks `messages[i + 1]` (the literal next array element) for the matching Skill tool_use call. It does not skip over an intervening isMeta/isSidechain 'user'-typed line, which this codebase's own conversation-splitter logic (claude.conversations-processor.ts) treats as a known, recurring transcript phenomenon.
findings.impact: In a real session where such a line interposes between a skill-backed slash command and the assistant's actual Skill tool_use reply, the lookahead finds no match and the command is still double-counted as both a command and a skill — silently reproducing the exact EPMCDME-17201 bug this change is meant to fix, in a shape the new unit tests (which never include an interposed line) cannot catch.
findings.recommendation: Either confirm (from real transcript samples or Claude Code's documented behavior) that no line can ever interpose between a skill-dispatching command and its Skill tool_use reply, and record that as an explicit invariant/comment, or widen the lookahead to skip forward past non-substantive lines (isMeta/isSidechain) to the next genuine assistant/user line before giving up.

findings.problem: Task 1's plan (Review Focus) explicitly requires a test proving a <command-name> tag lacking the <command-message> sibling is not treated as a genuine wrapper 'in either fix'. The pre-existing matchCommandNames gate (unchanged by this diff) is covered by a prior test, but the new wrappedCommandName/countTurns path has no dedicated test for this case.
findings.impact: No regression safety net if a future change accidentally makes wrappedCommandName match on a bare <command-name> mention (e.g. documentation/prose containing the literal text '/model'), which would wrongly exclude that line from Turns.
findings.recommendation: Add a countTurns test asserting a user line containing `<command-name>/model</command-name>` with no `<command-message>` sibling still counts as a turn (proves the sibling-gate, not just the denylist membership, is exercised on the new path).
